Customer header and Africa-first demo Service photography

Focused presentation/demo-data pass · October 2, 2026 · AgendaAlly

Scope held: no Shop hero/content redesign; no booking, commerce, Maps, permissions or ranking changes; no demographic application fields. No real bookings, orders, payments, payouts, refunds or provider activations were created.

Header findings and implementation

  • Position: the prior viewport-wide navigation used fixed search sizing and separated logo/action blocks rather than one flexible centered group. Its header framing did not match the centered Shop content. The old wordmark box was also undersized; increasing width alone would not resolve the composition.
  • Optical-size audit: approved PNG canvas 2172 × 724; visible artwork 2081 × 659 at (63,41). The artwork occupies about 95.8% of the horizontal canvas. Padding was minor, not the principal cause. No crop derivative or artwork redesign was needed.
  • Authoritative implementation: shared NavigationHeader, header-scoped SearchField hooks, and coherent logo sizing in the other shared Customer header. No absolute logo positioning or Shop-only workaround.
  • Desktop: centered maximum width 1220px; 156px image box, approximately 149.5px visible artwork; flexible/min-width-zero Search and balanced right actions. Measured logo-to-Search gap about 29px at 1440px. Header height 72px; final search group height 52px.
  • Tablet: 132px wordmark box, reduced gaps, flexible Search, existing responsive action controls. Header height 66px. Icon/label spacing and nested Date/Time padding are corrected; fields do not overlap.
  • Mobile: native back/navigation and responsive action treatment retained on Shop/booking pages, with desktop Search hidden. Other shared native header retains its existing small-brand architecture; no full desktop navigation forced into mobile. Shop header height 60px at 390px.
  • Footer branding and all Shop sections were left untouched. The mock's signed-in account/avatar and cart badge are not fabricated in the anonymous acceptance session.

Approved mock versus final native desktop

Responsive acceptance

  • Desktop PASS: readable full wordmark; moderate intentional gap; centered content relationship; prominent Search; actions fit; no overlap or horizontal overflow.
  • Tablet header PASS: readable branding, responsive spacing, usable-sized controls, no overlap or header overflow at 820px and 768px. The settled 820px whole page also passed.
  • 768px whole Shop page FAIL: existing Shop-body content still produces horizontal overflow even when the header is hidden. This is not presented as a whole-page pass. The Shop body is outside this approved correction and was not altered.
  • Mobile PASS (390px Shop): native back/action navigation, no squeezed desktop wordmark, no forced desktop Search and no horizontal overflow.

Service photography audit

  • 51 existing seeded Services reviewed; 19 placements retained, 32 replaced. Fifteen distinct final image assets: seven retained originals and eight new Pexels assets. All 15 original reviewed files remain intact; the archive contains 23 source files, not 23 final selected assets.
  • Categories: Hair Care, Barbershop, Makeup/Bridal Makeup, Nail Care, Spa & Massage, Education (tutoring, exam preparation, language, music and computer/digital skills), and Tattoo/Piercing.
  • Editorial representation: 25 of 35 people-centered final Service placements (71.4%) use source descriptions explicitly identifying Black/African-American subjects. Seven of eleven distinct people-centered final assets (63.6%). These are placements/assets, not unique people.
  • People-centered count means recognizable customer/professional/instructor/learner scenes. Sixteen treatment-detail placements are excluded: hair-colour detail 7, massage detail 7, ear-piercing detail 1 and tattoo touch-up detail 1. No ethnicity is inferred from hands, hair or bodies. Source descriptions do not verify nationality, ethnicity, or that a photograph was taken in Africa.
  • Reuse is confined to the same seeded Service across the seven demo beauty businesses, not one photo assigned to unrelated Services. Different photographs cover the different Service activities; the related tutoring/language teaching scenes are not claimed to be different individuals.
  • No Service lacks a relevant photograph. An equally accurate reviewed source-described Black/African beard-grooming asset was not found; the relevant original beard-grooming photo was retained. No suitable source-verified representative massage-therapist scene was found; the replacement uses professional treatment detail instead. Nonexistent Services such as braiding, fitness or pedicure were not invented.
  • Natural diversity is retained in music instruction, beard grooming and relevant tattoo/piercing work. Makeup imagery depicts actual application, not a claim that the stock subject is an actual bride or an AgendaAlly customer.

Native media safety

  • No schema, migration, racial application fields, demographic ranking, category-to-photo runtime fallback or remote runtime hotlinks were introduced.
  • Seeder is limited to the explicitly opted-in, owned local development database and reviewed IDs, Shop ownership, English Service title and known seeded reference/bytes. Changed Vendor references, removals or physical bytes are protected; reviewed source checksums are mandatory.
  • Replacements use content-versioned native storage names. Associations remain Service-owned. Only that Service's obsolete association is replaced; shared/old blobs are not deleted.
  • First run: 32 Services updated, 32 native files added, 32 associations added, 19 already correct; 0 protected/missing skips and 0 Services created.
  • Second run: 0 updates, 0 files added, 0 associations added; all 51 already correct.
  • Direct integrity check: all 51 native files match their selected reviewed SHA-256; all 51 have exactly one matching Service-owned Gallery association. Service count 51 and Gallery count 66 are unchanged.
  • No legitimate Vendor media was overwritten. No financial records were created. Final table-count comparison found only ordinary browsing activity (user_activities 19 → 20) differing. Earlier post-seed comparison recorded 196 unaffected table hashes; the later bounded attempt to reproduce that snapshot's encoder did not establish a fresh full-table hash result, so it is not claimed as one.

Sources and licensing

Pexels was the only additional source. Each asset has its source page, license, byte size and SHA-256 in the reviewed manifest. Downloaded local files only; no runtime hotlinks. Pexels License permits this demo use subject to its terms, including no misleading endorsement and no resale of unaltered assets. Source labels support editorial curation, not verified personal attributes.

Verification

  • Focused PHPUnit PASS: native media/ownership/seed selection — 8 tests, 33 assertions. Includes portable native Service references, Gallery isolation and guarded/content-versioned seeding.
  • Image-origin regression PASS: node --test .migration-backup/web/utils/service-media-url.test.cjs — 5 tests. Explicit native development opt-in, production unchanged, external/cloud images unchanged, rejected noncanonical/private/signed paths and restricted loopback origin.
  • Customer TypeScript: passed after the typed header changes in the design implementation pass; subsequent modifications were CSS only. A later 60-second bounded repeat emitted no diagnostics but timed out and is not claimed as another completed pass. No full production build was run for this bounded correction.
  • Live media PASS: Le Sawa, Wouri, Learning Hub and Wouri Ink/Piercing. Waited for actual Service buttons and decoded image bytes rather than treating loading skeletons as acceptance. Native photos are 112 × 112 with object-fit cover; no broken seeded images. Hair Care and Academic Tutoring also verified on native booking pages with all six/five Service photos loaded.
  • Booking/add PASS: selected Haircut on the native Wouri booking page; exactly one native “Remove selected service” control appeared. This proves a local selection, not a submitted reservation. Continue/checkout/payment was not invoked.
  • Neutral fallback: unchanged renderer/source inspected; real placeholder resource returned HTTP 200. No seeded Service lacked an image, so a genuine missing-media browser case was NOT EXERCISED; no media was deliberately removed to manufacture it.
  • Other Customer headers: homepage, Businesses, Specialists, Product browsing and empty Cart observed during the shared-header route sweep. This was header acceptance, not product/cart/checkout functional testing. Login was rechecked successfully after preview recovery; its native form and header rendered. No sign-in was performed.
  • Cold compilation of the broader route sweep exhausted preview resources and interrupted the initial login attempt. Customer preview was recovered, final changed flows rechecked, and unused Admin preview temporarily paused for verification. No shared recorder/editor processes were killed.

Remaining limitations and stop boundary

  • Existing whole-Shop-page overflow at 768px; header itself fits. No Shop content redesign was performed.
  • Genuine missing-image fallback was not encountered; source/resource checked only.
  • No authenticated account/menu, real booking, real checkout/payment, or full production build acceptance is claimed.
  • Later TypeScript repeat timed out; earlier completed typed-code check is distinguished above.
  • Exact stock-subject nationality/ethnicity and photographic location are not verified.

Stopped after these two corrections. No additional workstream or follow-up tasks proposed.
